findings.message: Last round's B4 finding is still open, and this diff doesn't touch it. HR still has two rules for 'today'. addPerson, recordLeaver and the hourly status job now use the entity's own today, and refuse an entity with no time zone. But changePersonRun still sets a missing effectiveOn to UTC `today()`, and it allows person-level fields only when `on === today()` in UTC (change.ts:58). The in-force reads also use UTC today: `personByNo` (`employmentAt(today())`, records.ts:36), and getPerson, getEmployment and reportUserIds in contracts.ts. They also never refuse an entity with no zone, so the round-2 rule to fail closed covers only some of the callers. Fix: have change.ts and records.ts use `entityToday` for the person's legal entity: for the default effective date, for the person-level same-day check, and for the in-force employment read. Then extend the 109 'one today' table test to cover changePerson near midnight.
findings.scenario: A Sri Lanka entity at 2026-11-15 02:00 local time (2026-11-14 20:30 UTC). addPerson with no joinedOn stores joined_on 2026-11-15, status active. Straight after, changePerson on that person with a title and effectiveOn 2026-11-15 (their local today) is refused with 'title change today: leave out effectiveOn…', because UTC today is 2026-11-14. If effectiveOn is left out, the change is dated 2026-11-14, the day before the person joined.

findings.message: This test is meant to prove that `done` names the edited range and percent after confirm. It calls `addCard` directly with the edited values already in the input, so it never goes through the confirm path. If `rewordCard` stopped rebuilding the card from the edited input, this test would still pass. Fix: drive the edit through the engine's confirm path (the code that calls `rewordCard`) and assert on the stored action's `look.done`.
findings.scenario: Change rewordCard so it keeps the proposed look. The card then says 'Added … 40% Mar–May' after Through was edited to 2027-04 and percent to 60, and this test still passes.

findings.message: zoneNote catches every error from `entityOf` and returns its message as the card's note. That includes database errors, not just 'not found' and 'ambiguous'. A raw DB error message then shows on the card. In Postgres the failed statement also aborts the surrounding transaction, so the next query in that transaction fails with 'current transaction is aborted' and that error is the one reported. Fix: catch only entityOf's own lookup errors (not found or ambiguous) and let other errors propagate.
findings.scenario: entityOf's query fails, for example on a statement timeout. The card shows the raw Postgres message as the entity note, and the next query in the same tx fails with 'current transaction is aborted'.

findings.message: For an entity with no zone, the hourly status job leaves its people unchanged and puts the entity's name only in `result.unzoned`, which ends up in a new audit row every hour. Nobody is told about it. People added before this change with a future joined_on or left_on now stay 'joining', or not yet 'left', until someone happens to set the zone. Fix: send a notifications rule or an Admin attention item when `unzoned` is not empty. Don't rely only on the audit payload.
findings.scenario: An existing tenant has an AU entity with no entity_zone row and a person who joined on 2026-11-20. After the 20th the person is still 'joining' on every screen and in every contract read. The only trace is `unzoned:['…Pty Ltd']` in 24 audit rows a day.
